subject.title: feat(memory-core): optional cross-encoder rerank stage for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw publish this `MemoryRerankProvider` API, `memoryRerankProviders` manifest gate, exclusive single-slot model, and builtin-only qmd scope as the durable plugin contract?
rationale: The implementation looks technically plausible, but the change creates a public plugin SDK surface and commits maintainers to a product/API shape that automation cannot choose.

options.title: Approve This Seam
options.body: Accept the vendor-neutral, registration-based rerank provider API and require a clean rebase plus focused verification before merge.

options.title: Revise The Contract
options.body: Ask for a different shape, such as keyed/config-selected providers, a newer capability declaration mechanism, or explicit qmd parity before merge.

options.title: Defer Or Reject
options.body: Keep the RFC open and leave concrete reranker work to an external plugin until maintainers are ready to commit to a core SDK seam.

recommendation.title: Approve This Seam
recommendation.body: Accept the vendor-neutral, registration-based rerank provider API and require a clean rebase plus focused verification before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across memory architecture, plugin SDK, and manifest boundaries touched by the public contract decision.
